These links are chosen with students and independent readers in mind. They complement the texts; they do not replace reading them. Each site has its own terms and language: most are in English.

## Reference works

- [Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy](https://plato.stanford.edu/) — peer-reviewed articles on Plato, ancient philosophy and related themes. The best starting point for serious study.
- [Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy](https://iep.utm.edu/) — clear, accessible articles written by specialists, useful when you meet Plato for the first time.

## Texts and translations

- [Perseus / Scaife Viewer](https://scaife.perseus.org/) — Greek texts with English translations, morphological tools and stable references. Essential for close reading.
- [Ad Fontes Library](https://adfonteslibrary.org/) — a free library of Greek and Latin classics and the Church Fathers, with English translations alongside the original texts.
- [MIT Internet Classics Archive](https://classics.mit.edu/) — public-domain English translations of Plato and other ancient authors, for quick access.
- [Loeb Classical Library](https://www.loebclassics.com/) — bilingual Greek–English editions widely used in academic work. Access by subscription.
- [Thesaurus Linguae Graecae](https://stephanus.tlg.uci.edu/) — the reference digital corpus of Greek literature. Full access by subscription; free registration opens a selection of texts.
- [Logeion](https://logeion.uchicago.edu/) — the major Greek and Latin dictionaries, including Liddell–Scott–Jones, in one free search. Also available as a mobile app.

## Courses

- [Ancient Philosophy: Plato and His Predecessors (Coursera)](https://www.coursera.org/learn/plato) — a university course on Plato and the thinkers before him.
- [Open Yale Courses](https://oyc.yale.edu/) — free public lectures, including political philosophy with extended readings of Plato's *Republic*.

## Videos

- [Wireless Philosophy](https://www.wi-phi.com/) — short videos on philosophical problems, several of them drawn from Plato's dialogues.

## Podcasts

- [History of Philosophy Without Any Gaps](https://historyofphilosophy.net/) — a podcast on the history of philosophy from the Presocratics onward, with many episodes on Plato.
- [BBC In Our Time](https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b006qykl) — discussions with scholars on classical topics, including Plato, Socrates and ancient Athens.
